quizzes.title: Competing Claims over the Site
quizzes.passage:
The Bhojshala–Kamal Maula Complex is a medieval monument protected by the Archaeological Survey of India. Its identity has been contested for a long time, and the building is described differently in tradition, in later historical records and in modern legal proceedings. Accounts of the complex therefore draw on several strands of evidence that do not always agree.

According to tradition, the structure was built by a king whose name is still attached to the building. The term Bhojshala, however, did not come into use until a later date. It became linked to the building in the early twentieth century, when inscriptions found at the site drew attention to that name.

Later records describe a period of Muslim rule during which the building was reportedly adapted for use as a mosque. Excavations in the twentieth century also brought to light an intricately carved image, and its later history has become part of the wider debate over the site. Both communities have made claims about the building, and these claims have shaped the matter before the courts.

The case before the Madhya Pradesh High Court concerned the right to worship at the site. The court was asked to decide questions about worship rather than ownership.

questions.q: Who is traditionally credited with building the complex, and in which year?
questions.explanation: The booklet records Raja Bhoj as the builder of the site in 1034 AD.

questions.q: The carved image found at the site during excavations is currently housed where?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the idol is housed in the British Museum, London.

questions.q: In which year was the building reportedly converted into a mosque?
questions.explanation: The booklet reports the conversion in 1514 AD under Muslim rule.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The complex is known to Muslims as the Kamal Maula Mosque.
Reason (R): The name is associated with the Sufi saint Hazrat Maulana Kamaluddin Chishti.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The mosque's name is tied to the saint, so R explains A.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The complex is a medieval monument located in Dhar, Madhya Pradesh.
II. The carved image found at the site is housed in the National Museum, New Delhi.
III. The site was traditionally regarded as a centre of Sanskrit learning and scholarship.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while the image is in the British Museum, not New Delhi.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Inscriptions that linked the name Bhojshala to the building   ->   A. Mehmudshah Khilji
II. Original dedication of the building   ->   B. Hazrat Maulana Kamaluddin Chishti
III. Ruler under whom the building was reportedly converted   ->   C. KK Lele
IV. Sufi saint associated with the Kamal Maula Mosque   ->   D. Goddess Saraswati (Vagdevi)
questions.explanation: The inscriptions are linked to K.K. Lele, the building to Goddess Saraswati, the conversion to Mehmudshah Khilji and the saint to Kamaluddin Chishti.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Hindus claim the site as a Saraswati temple.
II. Muslims identify the structure as the Kamal Maula Mosque.
III. The building was converted into a mosque in 1192 AD under Muhammad Ghori.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while the conversion year and ruler in III do not.

quizzes.title: Dates, Names and Places of the Site
quizzes.passage:
The Bhojshala–Kamal Maula Complex is a medieval monument protected by the Archaeological Survey of India. Hindus and Muslims describe the site differently. Tradition links the structure to Raja Bhoj, a ruler whose name is still attached to the building. The term Bhojshala, however, came into use only in the early twentieth century, after inscriptions were found at the site. Traditionally, the site was also regarded as a centre of Sanskrit learning and scholarship.

Later historical records describe a phase of Muslim rule in which the building was reportedly converted into a mosque. Muslims call the structure the Kamal Maula Mosque, a name linked to a Sufi figure. An intricately carved image found during twentieth-century excavations is now kept in a museum abroad, and its location has become part of the wider debate.

An ASI order issued in 2003 had allowed both communities to worship at the site on separate designated days, but the Madhya Pradesh High Court later quashed that order. The case before the court concerned the right to worship at the site. The court also directed the state government to consider applications for suitable alternative land within the town for a mosque or prayer site. The dispute has since been argued in courts and in public discussion.

questions.q: In which year does the booklet date the construction of the building by Raja Bhoj? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Raja Bhoj built the site in 1034 AD.

questions.q: In which year was the building reportedly converted into a mosque? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet reports a conversion in 1514 AD under Muslim rule.

questions.q: Which scholar's name is attached to the inscriptions that linked the name Bhojshala to the building? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the inscriptions found at the site were by KK Lele.

questions.q: In which city is the carved image found at the site now kept? (city)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the idol is housed in the British Museum, London.

questions.q: Which Sufi saint is associated with the Kamal Maula Mosque? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet links the Kamal Maula Mosque to Sufi saint Hazrat Maulana Kamaluddin Chishti.

questions.q: In which city is the monument located? (city)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the medieval ASI-protected monument is located in Dhar, Madhya Pradesh.

questions.q: Which goddess was the building originally believed to be dedicated to? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the structure is believed to have originally functioned as a temple of Goddess Saraswati (Vagdevi).

quizzes.title: Architecture and Inscriptions
quizzes.passage:
The Bhojshala–Kamal Maula Complex preserves structural remains and carved inscriptions that help historians study the site. The remains include a hall whose plan is typical of a particular kind of Hindu temple architecture. The inscriptions are among the most informative features of the complex, and several of them are cut into stone.

Some inscriptions are carved on pillars in a chart-like arrangement that appears designed to teach learners. Others are cut into stone slabs on the walls, where verses honour an avatar of a major Hindu deity. Other inscriptions name several rulers, which connects the site to the wider dynastic history of the region.

The inscriptions also refer to a Sanskrit drama named Karpuramanjari, which links the site to literary history. The Madhya Pradesh High Court later considered the site's history in a legal case, and the High Court has declared the site a Hindu temple. The Places of Worship Act, 1991 was also examined, since the court considered whether it applied to the complex at all.

The Archaeological Survey of India holds full supervisory, management and administrative control over the property. Its role covers regulating religious access and preserving the monument. The complex is a medieval monument that remains under the protection of the Archaeological Survey of India.

questions.q: Remains at the site indicate a hall of which architectural style, characteristic of Hindu temples?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the structural remains indicate a Mandapa-style hall, characteristic of Hindu temple architecture.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The pillar inscriptions at the site teach Sanskrit grammar to learners.
Reason (R): The Sarpabandha inscriptions chart the Sanskrit alphabet, noun and verb terminations, and the ten tenses and moods of Sanskrit grammar.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: R gives the content of the pillar inscriptions, which explains why A holds.

questions.q: In which language are the two odes to Kurma Avatara composed?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the odes on the walls are composed in Prakrit.

questions.q: Which author wrote the Sanskrit drama Karpuramanjari, which is referenced at the site?
questions.explanation: The booklet names royal tutor Madana as the author of Karpuramanjari.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Founder of the Gurjara-Pratihara Empire   ->   A. Kannauj (Mahodaya)
II. Capital of the Gurjara-Pratihara Empire   ->   B. Ashadhara
III. Most illustrious emperor of the Gurjara-Pratihara Empire   ->   C. Nagabhata I
IV. Jain scholar linked to the royal tutor Madana   ->   D. Raja Bhoj (Mihir Bhoja)
questions.explanation: Nagabhata I founded the empire, Kannauj was its capital, Raja Bhoj was its most illustrious emperor and Ashadhara was Madana's teacher.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Pratiharas were engaged in a tripartite struggle against the Palas of Bengal and the Rashtrakutas of the Deccan.
II. Raja Bhoj assumed the title Adivaraha, meaning the Boar incarnation of Vishnu.
III. The two odes to Kurma Avatara are composed in Pali.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while the odes are composed in Prakrit, not Pali.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Paramara rulers Udayaditya and Naravarman are mentioned in the inscriptions.
II. The Sarpabandha inscriptions chart the ten tenses and moods of Sanskrit grammar.
III. Nagabhata I founded the Gurjara-Pratihara Empire in 1514 AD.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while Nagabhata I's dates are 730-756 AD, not 1514 AD.

quizzes.title: Structure, Dynasty and Verse
quizzes.passage:
The Bhojshala–Kamal Maula Complex contains structural remains, carved pillars and stone slabs that together document parts of its history. The architectural remains point to a hall of a type found in Hindu temple buildings. The site is also known for a set of pillar inscriptions arranged to serve as a learning chart for students of an ancient classical language. The site uniquely preserves this kind of pillar inscription, which makes it a notable example of its type.

Verses cut into the walls honour one of the avatars of Lord Vishnu, and they are composed in an ancient Indian language. The inscriptions also name several rulers who governed the region in earlier centuries, which links the complex to a wider political past.

The site is additionally associated with the Sanskrit drama Karpuramanjari, which is referenced in its inscriptions. The Archaeological Survey of India holds administrative control over the property, including the management of affairs related to Sanskrit learning at the site. The Madhya Pradesh High Court has declared the site a Hindu temple, based on findings from a survey conducted by the Archaeological Survey of India. The site is also classed as an ancient monument under national heritage law. This is recorded in the account of the site's inscriptions.

questions.q: What type of hall do the architectural remains indicate? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the structural remains indicate a Mandapa-style hall.

questions.q: How many Sarpabandha pillar inscriptions does the site uniquely preserve? (number)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the site uniquely preserves 2 Sarpabandha pillar inscriptions.

questions.q: How many tenses and moods of Sanskrit grammar do the Sarpabandha inscriptions chart? (number)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the inscriptions chart the ten tenses and moods of Sanskrit grammar.

questions.q: Which dynasty's rulers, such as Udayaditya and Naravarman, are named in the inscriptions? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Sanskrit and Pali inscriptions mention Paramara rulers such as Udayaditya and Naravarman.

questions.q: Which avatar of Lord Vishnu are the odes on the walls dedicated to? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says two odes on the walls are dedicated to Kurma Avatara, the Tortoise Incarnation of Vishnu.

questions.q: What was the capital of the Gurjara-Pratihara Empire? (city)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives Kannauj (Mahodaya) as the capital of the Gurjara-Pratihara Empire.

questions.q: Nagabhata I is listed as the founder of which empire? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Nagabhata I (730-756 AD) as the founder of the Gurjara-Pratihara Empire.
